label: Digitally Immersed & Emotionally Distressed
summary: This profile represents highly educated women who spend more than 5 hours daily online and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. With a UCLA-8 loneliness mean of 1.74, PHQ-9 depression mean of 1.75, and notably high GAD-7 anxiety mean of 2.17, this group consistently scores above average on all three distress indicators. Their extensive screen time may both reflect and reinforce emotional difficulties, suggesting a pattern where digital immersion coexists with significant psychological burden.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, more than 5 hours of daily screen/internet use
behavior_markers: Elevated loneliness despite high connectivity and screen time
Highest anxiety levels among profiles (GAD-7 mean 2.17)
Extended daily digital engagement exceeding 5 hours
Potential reliance on online activity as a coping or avoidance mechanism
tone: Concerned and clinically attentive, highlighting the co-occurrence of heavy digital use and multi-dimensional emotional distress

label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report lower levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms compared to other groups. With UCLA-8 loneliness, PHQ-9 depression, and GAD-7 anxiety scores all well below scale midpoints, these individuals demonstrate generally positive psychological well-being across all three measured dimensions.
demographic_anchor: Male, holding a graduate degree or above, with 1–3 hours of daily screen/internet use
behavior_markers: Reports minimal loneliness (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 0.77, near floor)
Exhibits very low depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.33)
Maintains moderate and limited daily screen or internet use (1–3 hours)
Represents a relatively sizable subgroup (n = 150) suggesting a common well-functioning profile

label: Lonely but Emotionally Resilient
summary: This profile captures respondents who report notably elevated loneliness yet maintain relatively low levels of depressive and anxiety symptoms. Despite feeling socially disconnected, they appear to manage their emotional well-being without significant clinical distress, suggesting a pattern where subjective loneliness does not automatically translate into broader psychological impairment.
demographic_anchor: Predominantly female, holding graduate-level or higher education, reporting 1–3 hours of daily social-media or screen-related activity
behavior_markers: Elevated loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 1.30) indicating moderate-to-high perceived social isolation
Low depressive symptom burden (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.86) well below clinical thresholds
Low anxiety symptom burden (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.91) suggesting minimal generalized worry
Moderate daily screen or social-media use (1–3 hours), neither extremely low nor high
Possible reliance on coping strategies or academic/professional engagement that buffers against depression and anxiety despite social disconnection
tone: Quietly isolated yet psychologically stable; reflective and self-sufficient rather than distressed
